sourceDate.text: Tang Qujiang Lord Zhang (Zhang Jiuling era)
before Sun Che adulthood / Yuantong context
court selecting magistrates after Wu Ke mourning

units.zh: 古之君子，負經世之術，度時不可為，故高蹈以全其志。
units.en: Men of old who mastered the arts of governing the realm, when they judged that the times forbade action, would withdraw to lofty seclusion to keep their purpose intact.
units.literal: The gentleman of antiquity, bearing the arts of ordering the world, gauged that the times would not permit action, and therefore lifted his steps high to preserve his aspirations in full.

units.zh: 使得其時，未嘗不欲仕，仕而行所學，及物之功豈少哉。
units.en: Given the right moment, they were always ready to serve; and once in office they applied their learning—the good they did for the world was by no means small.
units.literal: If they obtained the right time, they had never been unwilling to serve in office; to serve and put what they had learned into practice—how could their achievements reaching others have been slight!

units.zh: 後世之士，其所蘊蓄或未至，而好以跡為高，當邦有道之時，且遁世離群，謂之隱士。
units.en: Scholars of later times, whose learning often fell short of the mark, nonetheless prided themselves on lofty withdrawal; even when the realm was well governed they would flee society and call themselves recluses.
units.literal: Scholars of later ages, whose stored learning had perhaps not yet arrived at completeness, yet loved to take conduct as loftiness; when the state had the Way, they yet withdrew from the world and separated from the crowd, and were called recluses.

units.zh: 世主亦苟取其名而強起之，及考其實，不如所聞，則曰「是欺世釣譽者也」，上下豈不兩失也哉！
units.en: Rulers too would seize on their reputations and compel them to office; when scrutiny showed them less than their fame, the verdict was "mere deceivers of the age fishing for praise"—a loss for ruler and subject alike.
units.literal: The lord of the age also would hastily take their names and force them to rise; when their reality was examined and did not match what was heard, then it was said, "These are those who deceive the world and fish for renown"—would not high and low alike lose doubly!

units.zh: 元之隱士亦多矣，如杜瑛遺執政書，暨張特立居官之政，則非徒隱者也，蓋其得時則行，可隱而隱，頗有古君子之風。
units.en: The Yuan had many men called recluses, yet figures such as Du Ying, who sent memorials to the chief ministers, and Zhang Teli, who governed ably in office, were not recluses in name only: they served when the moment allowed and withdrew when withdrawal was fitting—very much in the spirit of the ancients.
units.literal: Yuan recluses too were many; such as Du Ying leaving a letter to the chief ministers, and Zhang Teli's conduct in office—these were not mere recluses; broadly, when the time came they acted, and when withdrawal was possible they withdrew, bearing rather the air of the gentleman of antiquity.

units.zh: 而世主亦不強之使起，可謂兩得也已。
units.en: Nor did the rulers force such men to serve—so both sides gained their due.
units.literal: Yet the lord of the age also did not force them to rise—this may be called both sides gaining.

units.zh: 自是以隱逸稱者，蓋往往而有，今摭其可傳者，作《隱逸傳》。
units.en: From then on men famed for reclusion were not uncommon; here we collect those whose stories merit transmission and compose this "Biography of Recluses."
units.literal: From this time those styled by reclusion and withdrawal were perhaps often to be found; now their transmit-worthy cases are gathered to compose the "Biographies of Recluses."

units.zh: 杜瑛，字文玉，其先霸州信安人。
units.en: Du Ying, courtesy name Wenyu, came from a family originally of Xin'an in Bazhou.
units.literal: Du Ying, style name Wenyu, his ancestors were men of Xin'an in Bazhou.

units.zh: 父時昇，《金史》有傳。
units.en: His father Shi Sheng is recorded in the History of Jin.
units.literal: His father Shi Sheng has a biography in the History of Jin.

units.zh: 瑛長七尺，美鬚髯，氣貌魁偉。
units.en: Ying stood seven feet in height, with a fine beard and whiskers and a commanding, imposing presence.
units.literal: Ying was seven chi tall, with handsome beard and whiskers, his bearing and appearance imposing and grand.

units.zh: 金將亡，士猶以文辭規進取，瑛獨避地河南緱氏山中。
units.en: As the Jin dynasty neared its end, scholars still courted advancement through polished writing; Ying alone withdrew to the Goushi Mountains in Henan.
units.literal: When Jin was about to perish, scholars still used literary compositions to plot advancement; Ying alone avoided the land and went to the Goushi Mountains in Henan.

units.zh: 時兵後，文物凋喪，瑛搜訪諸書，盡讀之，讀輒不忘，而究其指趣，古今得失如指諸掌。
units.en: In the aftermath of war, learning lay in ruins; Ying sought out every book he could find and read them all, retaining whatever he read and probing their meaning until the rights and wrongs of past and present lay clear in his hand.
units.literal: At the time, after warfare, culture and artifacts had withered and been lost; Ying searched out and gathered all books, reading them through entirely; what he read he did not forget, and he plumbed their purport—gain and loss in past and present like pointing to the palm.

units.zh: 間關轉徙，教授汾、晉間。
units.en: After many hardships and wanderings, he taught in the Fen and Jin regions.
units.literal: Threading hardship and shifting from place to place, he taught between Fen and Jin.

units.zh: 中書粘合珪開府於相，瑛赴其聘，遂家焉。
units.en: When Ahekan Gui of the Central Secretariat established his headquarters at Xiangzhou, Ying accepted his invitation and settled there.
units.literal: The Central Secretariat's Ahekan Gui opened a headquarters at Xiang; Ying answered his invitation and thereupon made his home there.

units.zh: 與良田千畝，辭不受。
units.en: He was offered a thousand mu of fertile land but refused it.
units.literal: They gave him a thousand mu of fertile fields; he declined and did not accept.

units.zh: 術者言其所居下有藏金，家人欲發視，輒止之。
units.en: A geomancer said gold was buried beneath his dwelling; when his family wanted to dig, he always forbade it.
units.literal: A diviner said that beneath where he dwelt there was hidden gold; his household wished to dig and look, but he always stopped them.

units.zh: 後來居者果得黃金百斤，其不苟取如此。
units.en: Later occupants did in fact find a hundred jin of gold there—such was his refusal to take what was not rightfully his.
units.literal: Later those who dwelt there indeed obtained a hundred jin of yellow gold—such was his not taking what was not his due.

units.zh: 歲己未，世祖南伐至相，召見問計，瑛從容對曰：「漢、唐以還，人君所恃以為國者，法與兵、食三事而已。
units.en: In the jiwei year, Kublai Khan on his southern campaign reached Xiangzhou and summoned Ying to ask his counsel. Ying replied calmly: "Since Han and Tang, what rulers have relied on to sustain a state are only three things: law, arms, and grain.
units.literal: In the year jiwei, the Founder on his southern campaign reached Xiang, summoned him for audience and asked his plans; Ying answered at ease: "Since Han and Tang, what a ruler relies on to make a state is only three things: law, troops, and provisions.

units.zh: 國無法不立，人無食不生，亂無兵不守。
units.en: Without law a state cannot stand; without food the people cannot live; in chaos without arms nothing can be held.
units.literal: Without law a state cannot stand; without food people cannot live; in disorder without troops it cannot be guarded.

units.zh: 今宋皆蔑之，殆將亡矣，興之在聖主。
units.en: Song now scorns all three—it is near ruin; renewal rests with Your Sagely Majesty.
units.literal: Now Song treats all these with contempt—it will almost perish; the rise lies with the sage ruler.

units.zh: 若控襄樊之師，委戈下流，以搗其背，大業可定矣。」
units.en: Hold your forces at Xiangyang and Fancheng, then send troops down the river to strike Song from behind, and the great enterprise will be assured."
units.literal: If you hold the armies of Xiang and Fan, lay aside weapons and go downstream, to strike their rear, the great enterprise can be settled."

units.zh: 帝悅，曰：「儒者中乃有此人乎！」
units.en: The Emperor was pleased and said, "Among scholars there is actually such a man as this!"
units.literal: The Emperor was pleased and said: "Among Confucians there is actually such a person!"

units.zh: 瑛复勸帝數事，以謂事不如此，後當如彼。
units.en: Ying went on to counsel the Emperor on several points, warning that if matters were not handled one way now, they would turn out another way later.
units.literal: Ying again urged the Emperor on several matters, saying that if things were not thus now, later they would be as that.

units.zh: 帝納之，心賢瑛，謂可大用，命從行，以疾弗果。
units.en: The Emperor accepted his advice, came to esteem Ying highly, and judged him fit for great office; he ordered Ying to accompany the campaign, but illness prevented it.
units.literal: The Emperor accepted it, in his heart esteemed Ying, deemed him fit for great employment, ordered him to follow on the march, but because of illness it did not come to pass.

units.zh: 中統初，詔徵瑛。
units.en: Early in the Zhongtong era, an imperial summons called for Ying.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhongtong, an edict summoned Ying.

units.zh: 時王文統方用事，辭不就。
units.en: Wang Wentong was then in power at court; Ying declined and did not accept office.
units.literal: At the time Wang Wentong was just then in power; he declined and did not go.

units.zh: 左丞張文謙宣撫河北，奏為懷孟、彰德、大名等路提舉學校官，又辭，遺執政書，其略曰：「先王之道不明，異端邪說害之也，橫流奔放，天理不絕如線。
units.en: Left Assistant Zhang Wenqian, pacification commissioner of Hebei, recommended him as supervisor of schools for the Huaimeng, Zhangde, Daming, and other circuits; Ying declined again and sent the chief ministers a letter that read in part: "The Way of the ancient kings is obscured, harmed by heterodox teachings; doctrines run wild, and the moral order hangs by a thread.
units.literal: Left Assistant Zhang Wenqian as Pacification Commissioner of Hebei memorialized to make him Supervisor of Schools for the Huaimeng, Zhangde, Daming, and other circuits; again he declined, leaving a letter to the chief ministers, its gist saying: "The Way of the former kings is not clear; heterodox and perverse doctrines harm it; flowing wildly and rushing forth, Heavenly principle hangs by a thread not severed.

units.zh: 今天子神聖，俊乂輻輳，言納計用，先王之禮樂教化，興明修復，維其時矣。
units.en: Today the Son of Heaven is sage, the worthy gather at court, and counsel is heeded—this is the moment to revive and restore the rites, music, and civilizing teachings of the ancient kings.
units.literal: Now the Son of Heaven is divine and sage, the worthy and able gather like wheel spokes; words are received and plans employed—the former kings' rites, music, and civilizing transformation may be raised bright and repaired and restored; this is the time.

units.zh: 若夫簿書期會，文法末節，漢、唐猶不屑也，執事者因陋就簡，此焉是務，良可惜哉！
units.en: Yet ledgers, deadlines, and petty legal formalities—even Han and Tang scorned such things—while those in office cling to the shabby and the expedient. How regrettable!
units.literal: As for ledgers and scheduled meetings, literary regulations and minor points—even Han and Tang still disdained these; those in charge, following what is shabby and settling for what is simple, make this their task—truly pitiable!

units.zh: 夫善始者未必善終，今不能溯流求源，明法正俗，育材興化，以拯數百千年之禍，僕恐後日之弊，將有不可勝言者矣。」
units.en: A good beginning does not guarantee a good end. If we cannot trace the stream to its source—clarify law, rectify custom, nurture talent, and revive civilization—to redeem centuries of ruin, I fear the evils of later days will be beyond telling."
units.literal: Those who begin well need not end well; now if one cannot go upstream to seek the source, clarify law and rectify custom, nurture talent and raise transformation, to rescue the calamity of several hundred or a thousand years—I fear later days' abuses will have what cannot be spoken in full."

units.zh: 人或勉之仕，則曰：「後世去古雖遠，而先王之所設施，本末先後，猶可考見，故為政者莫先於復古。
units.en: When others urged him to serve, he said: "Though our age is far from antiquity, what the ancient kings instituted—its sequence and structure—can still be studied; for anyone who would govern, nothing comes before restoring the ancient ways.
units.literal: When some urged him to take office, he said: "Later ages though far from antiquity, yet what the former kings established—root and branch, before and after—can still be examined and seen; therefore for one who governs nothing comes before returning to antiquity.

units.zh: 苟因習舊弊，以求合乎先王之意，不亦難乎！
units.en: Yet to cling to entrenched abuses and still hope to match the intent of the ancient kings—is that not impossible?
units.literal: If one merely follows accustomed old abuses, to seek to accord with the former kings' intent—is it not also difficult!

units.zh: 吾又不能隨時俯仰以赴機會，將焉用仕！」
units.en: Nor can I bend with the times to seize opportunity—what use would office be to me!"
units.literal: I also cannot bend and rise with the times to meet opportunity—of what use is taking office!"

units.zh: 於是杜門著書，一不以窮通得喪動其志，優游道藝，以終其身。
units.en: He then shut his doors and devoted himself to writing, never letting fortune or misfortune sway his purpose, and passed his days at ease in learning and the arts until he died.
units.literal: Thereupon he shut his door and wrote books, never once letting poverty or success, gain or loss move his will, at ease in the Way and the arts until his life's end.

units.zh: 年七十，遺命其子處立、處願曰：「吾即死，當表吾墓曰'緱山杜處士'。」
units.en: At seventy he instructed his sons Chuli and Chuyuan: "When I die, let my tombstone read 'Gentleman Du of Goushi Mountain.'"
units.literal: At age seventy, he left testamentary instructions to his sons Chuli and Chuyuan, saying: "When I am about to die, you should inscribe my tomb tablet 'Goushi Gentleman Du.'"

units.zh: 天歷中，贈資德大夫、翰林學士、上護軍，追封魏郡公，諡文獻。
units.en: In the Tianli reign he was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Virtuous Talent, Hanlin Academician, and Senior Guardian of the Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei Commandery, with the posthumous name Wenxian.
units.literal: In the Tianli era, posthumously granted Grand Master of Virtuous Talent, Hanlin Academician, and Senior Guardian of the Army; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Wei Commandery, posthumous name Wenxian.

units.zh: 所著書曰《春秋地理原委》十卷、《語孟旁通》八卷、《皇極引用》八卷、《皇極疑事》四卷、《極學》十卷、《律呂律曆禮樂雜志》三十卷、文集十卷。
units.en: His works included Origins of Spring and Autumn Geography (10 juan), Collateral Passages to the Analects and Mencius (8 juan), Supreme Ultimate Citations (8 juan), Supreme Ultimate Doubtful Matters (4 juan), Ultimate Learning (10 juan), Miscellaneous Records of Pitch Pipes, Calendars, Rites, and Music (30 juan), and collected writings (10 juan).
units.literal: Books he authored include Origins of Spring and Autumn Geography in ten juan, Analects and Mencius Collateral Passages in eight juan, Supreme Ultimate Citations in eight juan, Supreme Ultimate Doubtful Matters in four juan, Ultimate Learning in ten juan, Miscellaneous Records of Pitch Pipes, Calendars, Rites, and Music in thirty juan, and collected writings in ten juan.

units.zh: 其於律，則究其始，研其義，長短清濁，周徑積實，各以類分，取經史之說以實之，而折衷其是非。
units.en: On pitch pipes he traced their origins and probed their principles—length, pitch, circumference, diameter, and volume—classifying each type and testing classical and historical accounts to judge what was right and wrong.
units.literal: Regarding pitch pipes, he traced their beginnings and investigated their principles—long and short, clear and muddy, circumference, diameter, accumulated solid—each sorted by category; he took classical and historical explanations to substantiate them and weighed right and wrong.

units.zh: 其於歷，則謂造歷者皆從十一月甲子朔夜半冬至為曆元，獨邵子以為天開於子，取日甲月子、星甲辰子，為元會運世之數，無朔虛，無閏餘，率以三百六十為歲，而天地之盈虛，百物之消長，不能出乎其中矣。
units.en: On calendrics he noted that calendar-makers generally took the winter solstice at midnight on the jiazi day of the eleventh month's new moon as the epoch, whereas Master Shao Yong held that Heaven opens at zi and used jiazi for day, month, and star to derive the cycles of origin, meeting, movement, and age—without intercalary gaps, treating 360 as a standard year—yet the waxing and waning of heaven, earth, and all things could not escape this framework.
units.literal: Regarding the calendar, he said calendar-makers all take the first day of the eleventh month, jiazi new moon, midnight winter solstice as calendar origin; only Master Shao held that Heaven opens at zi, taking day jiazi month zi, star jiazi chen zi, as the numbers of origin, meeting, movement, and world-age—without new-moon void, without intercalary remainder, uniformly taking 360 as the year—yet Heaven and Earth's fullness and emptiness, the waxing and waning of the hundred things, cannot lie outside this.

units.zh: 論閉物開物，則曰開於己，閉於戊；
units.en: On the closing and opening of things, he held that they open at ji and close at wu;
units.literal: Discussing closing things and opening things, he said they open at ji and close at wu;

units.zh: 五，天之中也；
units.en: five is the center of Heaven;
units.literal: Five is Heaven's center;

units.zh: 六，地之中也；
units.en: six is the center of Earth;
units.literal: Six is Earth's center;

units.zh: 戊己，月之中星也。
units.en: wu and ji are the central stars of the Moon.
units.literal: Wu and ji are the Moon's central stars.

units.zh: 又分卦配之紀年，金之大定庚寅，交小過之初六；
units.en: He also matched hexagrams to years: the Jin Dading gengyin year corresponded to the initial six line of Xiao Guo (Small Exceeding);
units.literal: He also assigned hexagrams to years for chronology: Jin's Dading gengyin year corresponded to the initial six of Xiao Guo;

units.zh: 國朝之甲寅三月二十有三日寅時，交小過之九四。
units.en: and our dynasty's jiayin year, on the twenty-third day of the third month at the yin hour, corresponded to the nine-four line of Xiao Guo.
units.literal: Our dynasty's jiayin year, the twenty-third day of the third month at the yin hour, corresponded to the nine-four of Xiao Guo.

units.zh: 多先儒所未發，掇其要著於篇云。
units.en: Much of this earlier scholars had not articulated; here the essentials are gathered for this account.
units.literal: Much of this earlier Confucians had not brought forth; he gathered the essentials and set them down in this chapter.

units.zh: 張特立，字文舉，東明人。
units.en: Zhang Teli, courtesy name Wenju, was from Dongming.
units.literal: Zhang Teli, style name Wenju, was a man of Dongming.

units.zh: 初名永，避金衛紹王諱，易今名。
units.en: His original name was Yong; to avoid the taboo name of the Jin Prince Shao of Wei, he adopted his present name.
units.literal: His original name was Yong; to avoid the taboo of Jin's Prince Shao of Wei, he changed to his present name.

units.zh: 中泰和進士，為偃師主簿。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the Taihe era and became chief clerk of Yanshi.
units.literal: In the Taihe era he passed the jinshi examination and served as chief clerk of Yanshi.

units.zh: 改宣德州司候。
units.en: He was later appointed judicial officer of Xuande Prefecture.
units.literal: He was transferred to be judicial officer of Xuande Prefecture.

units.zh: 州多金國戚，號難治，特立至官，俱往謁之。
units.en: The prefecture had many Jin imperial kinsmen and was notoriously hard to govern; when Teli took office, they all came to pay their respects.
units.literal: The prefecture had many Jin imperial clansmen and was called hard to govern; when Teli arrived in office, all went to pay court calls on him.

units.zh: 有五將軍率家奴劫民群羊，特立命大索閭里，遂過將軍家，溫言誘之曰：「將軍宅寧有盜羊者邪，聊視之以杜眾口。」
units.en: A general known as the Fifth General had his household slaves seize villagers' flocks; Teli ordered a thorough search of the neighborhood and then called at the general's house, saying mildly, "Surely there are no sheep thieves in your residence, General—but let us have a look to silence gossip."
units.literal: There was a Fifth General who led household slaves to rob the people's flocks of sheep; Teli ordered a great search through the lanes and quarters, then passed by the general's house and with gentle words coaxed him, saying: "In the general's residence could there be sheep thieves? Let us just look to silence the crowd's mouths."

units.zh: 潛使人索其後庭，得羊數十。
units.en: He secretly had the rear courtyard searched and found several dozen sheep.
units.literal: Secretly he sent men to search the rear courtyard and obtained several tens of sheep.

units.zh: 遂縛其奴繫獄，其子匿他舍，捕得之，以近族得減死論。
units.en: He bound the slaves and jailed them; the son, hiding elsewhere, was captured and, because of near kinship, received a reduced sentence short of death.
units.literal: Thereupon he bound the slaves and imprisoned them; the son hid in another lodging and was captured; because of near kinship he received reduced sentence from death.

units.zh: 豪貴由是遵法，民賴以全。
units.en: The powerful henceforth obeyed the law, and the people were protected.
units.literal: The powerful and noble from this obeyed the law, and the people relied on this to be preserved whole.

units.zh: 正大初，遷洛陽令。
units.en: Early in the Zhengda era he was appointed magistrate of Luoyang.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhengda, he was transferred to magistrate of Luoyang.

units.zh: 時軍旅數起，郡縣窘迫，東帥紇石烈牙兀䚟又侮慢儒士。
units.en: Armies marched repeatedly, counties were strapped for resources, and the eastern commander He-shilie Yarucha treated scholars with contempt.
units.literal: At the time armies and campaigns arose repeatedly, commanderies and counties were pressed tight, and the eastern commander He-shilie Yarucha also insulted and slighted Confucian scholars.

units.zh: 會移鎮陝右，道經洛陽，見特立淳古，不禮之，遽責令治糗具，期三日足，後期如軍法。
units.en: When he was transferred to garrison western Shaanxi and passed through Luoyang, he found Teli plain and unassuming, showed him no courtesy, and abruptly ordered him to supply army rations within three days on pain of military law.
units.literal: It happened he was transferred to garrison the right of Shaanxi, his route passing Luoyang; seeing Teli's plain antiquity, he did not treat him with ritual, but abruptly charged him to prepare dried provisions, fixing three days to be sufficient—after the deadline as military law.

units.zh: 縣民素賢特立，爭輸於庭，帥大奇之。
units.en: The people of the county, who had long admired Teli, rushed to deliver supplies to the magistrate's court, and the commander was astonished.
units.literal: The county people had long esteemed Teli and vied to deliver supplies in the courtyard; the commander was greatly astonished.

units.zh: 既而拜監察御史，首言世宗諸孫不宜幽囚；
units.en: He was soon appointed investigating censor and first memorialized that Emperor Shizong's grandsons should not be kept in confinement;
units.literal: Soon after he was appointed investigating censor and first said that Shizong's grandsons should not be held in secret imprisonment;

units.zh: 尚書右丞顏盞石魯與細民爭田，參知政事徒單兀典諂事近習，皆當罷黜。
units.en: that Right Assistant Minister Yanzhan Shilu was wrangling over land with commoners, and Participating Administrator Tushan Wudian was currying favor with the emperor's intimates—all should be removed from office.
units.literal: Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat Yanzhan Shilu contended for fields with common people, and Participating Administrator Tushan Wudian flattered and served those near at hand—all should be dismissed.

units.zh: 執政者忌之。
units.en: The chief ministers resented him.
units.literal: Those in power resented him.

units.zh: 會平章政事白撒犒軍陝西，特立又劾其掾不法。
units.en: When Grand Councilor Bai Sa went to reward the troops in Shaanxi, Teli again impeached his staff for misconduct.
units.literal: It happened that Grand Councilor Bai Sa was rewarding the army in Shaanxi; Teli again impeached his clerks for unlawful conduct.

units.zh: 白撒訴於世宗，言特立所言事失實，世宗宥之，遂歸田裡。
units.en: Bai Sa complained to Emperor Shizong that Teli's charges were false; the emperor pardoned Teli, who then retired to the countryside.
units.literal: Bai Sa complained to Shizong, saying Teli's stated matters were not factual; Shizong pardoned him, and he thereupon returned to fields and villages.

units.zh: 特立通程氏《易》，晚教授諸生，東平嚴實每加禮焉。
units.en: Teli mastered the Cheng school interpretation of the Changes; in later years he taught students, and Yan Shi of Dongping always treated him with respect.
units.literal: Teli was versed in the Cheng school Changes; in his later years he taught students, and Dongping's Yan Shi always showed him added courtesy.

units.zh: 歲丙午，世祖在潛邸受王印，首傳旨諭特立曰：「前監察御史張特立，養素丘園，易代如一，今年幾七十，研究聖經，宜錫嘉名，以光潛德，可特賜號曰中庸先生。」
units.en: In the bingwu year, when Kublai received the princely seal in his residence, he first sent word to Teli: "The former censor Zhang Teli has lived in rustic seclusion through the change of dynasties unchanged; he is nearly seventy and devoted to the classics. Let an honorable title glorify his hidden virtue: grant him specially the name Master of the Mean (Zhongyong)."
units.literal: In the bingwu year, the Founder in his princely residence received the princely seal; he first transmitted an order instructing Teli: "Former investigating censor Zhang Teli, nurturing simplicity in hill and garden, the change of dynasties as one, this year nearly seventy, investigating the sage classics—fitting to bestow an excellent name to glorify hidden virtue; he may be specially granted the title Master of the Mean."

units.zh: 又諭曰：「先生年老目病，不能就道，故令趙寶臣諭意，且名其讀書之堂曰麗澤。」
units.en: He added: "The Master is aged and his eyes are failing and cannot travel; Zhao Baochen is therefore sent to convey my wishes and to name his study the Hall of Beautiful Marsh (Lize)."
units.literal: He further instructed: "The master is old and his eyes are ill; he cannot come on the road—therefore Zhao Baochen is sent to convey the intent, and moreover to name his hall of reading Li Ze (Beautiful Marsh)."

units.zh: 壬子歲，复降璽書諭特立曰：「白首窮經，誨人不倦，無過不及，學者宗之，昔已賜嘉名，今復諭意。」
units.en: In the renzi year another imperial letter reached him: "White-haired, you exhaust the classics and teach without weariness, neither exceeding nor falling short—scholars look to you as their model. An honorable name was granted before; I send my regards again."
units.literal: In the renzi year, again an imperial sealed letter was sent instructing Teli: "White-haired, exhausting the classics, teaching people without weariness, neither excess nor shortfall—scholars take him as their model; formerly an excellent name was already granted; now again the intent is conveyed."

units.zh: 癸丑，特立卒，年七十五。
units.en: In guichou Teli died at the age of seventy-five.
units.literal: In guichou, Teli died, age seventy-five.

units.zh: 中統二年，詔曰：「中庸先生學有淵源，行無瑕玷，雖經喪亂，不改故常，未遂丘園之賁，俄興窀穸之悲。
units.en: In the second year of Zhongtong an edict read: "Master of the Mean—his learning ran deep, his conduct without blemish; though he lived through chaos he did not change his ways; he had not yet received the full honor due a recluse when suddenly the grief of burial arose.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong, an edict said: "Master of the Mean—learning has deep springs, conduct without flaw; though passing through mourning and disorder, he did not alter his old constancy; he had not yet attained the adornment of hill and garden, when suddenly arose the grief of the burial mound.

units.zh: 可復賜前號，以彰寵數。」
units.en: Let his former title be granted again to display imperial favor."
units.literal: He may again be granted the former title to display imperial favor."

units.zh: 特立所著書有《易集說》、《歷年系事記》。
units.en: Teli's works included Collected Explanations of the Changes and Annals of Events by Year.
units.literal: Books Teli authored include Collected Explanations of the Changes and Annals of Events by Year.

units.zh: 杜本，字伯原，其先居京兆，後徙天台，又徙臨江之清江，今為清江人。
units.en: Du Ben, courtesy name Boyuan, came from a family that had lived in Jingzhao, later moved to Tiantai, and then to Qingjiang in Linjiang; he was now regarded as a native of Qingjiang.
units.literal: Du Ben, style name Boyuan, his ancestors dwelt in Jingzhao, later moved to Tiantai, again moved to Qingjiang in Linjiang—now he is a man of Qingjiang.

units.zh: 本博學，善屬文。
units.en: Ben was widely learned and a skilled writer.
units.literal: Ben was broadly learned and skilled at literary composition.

units.zh: 江浙行省丞相忽剌術得其所上《救荒策》，大奇之，及入為御史大夫，力荐於武宗。
units.en: Grand Councilor Hulashu of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat was greatly impressed by Ben's "Policy for Relieving Famine"; when Hulashu became censor-in-chief, he strongly recommended Ben to Emperor Wuzong.
units.literal: The Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat grand councilor Hulashu obtained his submitted "Famine Relief Policy" and was greatly struck by it; when he entered office as censor-in-chief, he strongly recommended him to Wuzong.

units.zh: 嘗被召至京師，未幾歸隱武夷山中。
units.en: He was once summoned to the capital but soon withdrew to seclusion in the Wuyi Mountains.
units.literal: He was once summoned to the capital; before long he returned to seclusion in the Wuyi Mountains.

units.zh: 文宗在江南時，聞其名，及即位，以幣征之，不起。
units.en: When Wenzong was in the south he heard of Ben; after his accession he sent gifts to summon him, but Ben did not accept.
units.literal: When Wenzong was in Jiangnan he heard his name; upon taking the throne he sent gifts to summon him—he did not rise.

units.zh: 至正三年，右丞相脫脫以隱士薦，詔遣使賜以金織文幣、上尊酒，召為翰林待制、奉議大夫，兼國史院編修官。
units.en: In Zhizheng 3, Right Grand Councilor Toghto recommended him as a recluse; the court sent envoys with brocade and fine wine and summoned him as Hanlin awaiting edict, Gentleman for Discussion, and compiler at the History Office.
units.literal: In the third year of Zhizheng, Right Grand Councilor Toghto recommended him as a recluse; an edict sent envoys bestowing gold-woven patterned silks and superior libation wine, summoning him as Hanlin awaiting edict, Gentleman for Discussion, and concurrently History Office compiler.

units.zh: 使者致君、相意，趣之行。
units.en: The envoys conveyed the emperor's and the minister's wishes and pressed him to depart.
units.literal: The envoys conveyed the ruler's and minister's intent, urging him to go.

units.zh: 至杭州，稱疾固辭，而致書於丞相曰：「以萬事合為一理，以萬民合為一心，以千載合為一日，以四海合為一家，則可言制禮作樂，而躋五帝三王之盛矣。」
units.en: At Hangzhou he pleaded illness and firmly declined, writing to the grand councilor: "When the myriad affairs are united in one principle, the myriad people in one heart, a thousand years in a single day, and the four seas in one household—then one may speak of making rites and music and attaining the glory of the Five Emperors and Three Kings."
units.literal: Reaching Hangzhou, he claimed illness and firmly declined, yet sent a letter to the grand councilor saying: "Take the ten thousand affairs and unite them as one principle, the ten thousand people as one heart, a thousand years as one day, the four seas as one family—then one may speak of instituting rites and composing music and ascend to the splendor of the Five Emperors and Three Kings."

units.zh: 遂不行。
units.en: He did not go.
units.literal: He thereupon did not go.

units.zh: 本湛靜寡欲，無疾言遽色。
units.en: Ben was calm and abstemious, never speaking harshly or showing sudden anger.
units.literal: Ben was deep-still and few in desires, without hasty speech or sudden color.

units.zh: 與人交尤篤於義，有貧無以養親、無貲以為學者，皆濟之。
units.en: In friendship he was especially devoted to duty; he helped all who were too poor to support their parents or pay for their studies.
units.literal: In dealings with people he was especially earnest in righteousness; those poor without means to support parents, without funds to pursue learning—he all aided them.

units.zh: 平居書冊未嘗釋手。
units.en: In daily life he never put his books down.
units.literal: In ordinary life books were never released from his hand.

units.zh: 天文、地理、律曆、度數，靡不通究，尤工於篆隸。
units.en: He mastered astronomy, geography, calendrics, and mathematics, and was especially accomplished in seal and clerical calligraphy.
units.literal: Astronomy, geography, pitch pipes and calendars, measures and numbers—none he did not thoroughly investigate; he was especially skilled in seal and clerical scripts.

units.zh: 所著有《四經表義》、《六書通編》、《十原》等書，學者稱為清碧先生。
units.en: His works included Expositions of the Four Classics, Comprehensive Compilation of the Six Scripts, and Ten Origins; scholars called him Master Clear Jade (Qingbi).
units.literal: Works he authored include Expositions of the Four Classics, Comprehensive Compilation of the Six Scripts, Ten Origins, and other books; scholars called him Master Clear Jade.

units.zh: 至正十年卒，年七十有五。
units.en: He died in Zhizheng 10 at the age of seventy-five.
units.literal: In the tenth year of Zhizheng he died, age seventy-five.

units.zh: 時有張樞子長者，婺之金華人，亦屢徵不起。
units.en: At the time there was Zhang Shu, courtesy name Zichang, a man of Jinhua in Wu prefecture, who likewise refused repeated summons.
units.literal: At the time there was the elder Zhang Shu, a man of Jinhua in Wu—also repeatedly summoned and not rising.

units.zh: 樞幼聰慧，外家潘氏蓄書數万卷，樞盡取而讀之，過目輒不忘。
units.en: Shu was clever as a boy; his mother's Pan family kept tens of thousands of volumes, which he read through entirely, forgetting nothing he saw.
units.literal: Shu in youth was clever and intelligent; his maternal family's Pan clan stored books in several tens of thousands of juan; Shu took them all and read them—what passed his eyes he did not forget.

units.zh: 既長，肆筆成章，頃刻數千言。
units.en: When grown he could take up the brush and compose essays of several thousand words in moments.
units.literal: When grown, he took up the brush and formed compositions, in a moment several thousand words.

units.zh: 有問以古今沿革、政治得失、宇宙之分合、禮樂之廢興，以至帝號官名、歲月先後，歷歷如指諸掌。
units.en: Asked about historical change, political success and failure, cosmic cycles, the rise and fall of rites and music, or even imperial titles, offices, and chronology, he answered with the clarity of facts held in his palm.
units.literal: If asked about past and present evolution, political gain and loss, the cosmos's division and union, rites and music's abolition and rise—even to imperial titles, office names, years and months before and after—he laid them out clearly like pointing to the palm.

units.zh: 其為文，務推明經史，以扶翼教道，尤長於敘事。
units.en: In his writing he sought to illuminate the classics and histories to uphold the Way, and was especially gifted at narrative.
units.literal: His writing aimed to extend and clarify the classics and histories, to support and wing the teaching of the Way; he was especially skilled at narrative.

units.zh: 嘗取三國時事撰《漢本紀列傳》，附以《魏吳載記》，為《續後漢書》七十三卷。
units.en: He once compiled Han Basic Annals and Biographies from Three Kingdoms materials, with Wei and Wu Records appended, as a Continued History of Later Han in seventy-three juan.
units.literal: He once took Three Kingdoms affairs to compose Han Basic Annals and Biographies, appended with Wei and Wu Records, making Continued History of Later Han in seventy-three juan.

units.zh: 臨川危素稱其立義精密，可備勸講，朝廷取其書置宣文閣。
units.en: Wei Su of Linchuan praised its arguments as precise and fit for imperial lectures; the court placed the work in the Xuanwen Pavilion.
units.literal: Linchuan's Wei Su praised its established meanings as precise and dense, fit to supply exhortation and exposition; the court took his book and placed it in the Xuanwen Pavilion.

units.zh: 浙東部使者交薦之，前後章凡九上。
units.en: The Zhedong circuit envoy recommended him repeatedly, with nine memorials in all.
units.literal: The Zhedong circuit envoy repeatedly recommended him; memorials before and after totaled nine submitted.

units.zh: 至正三年，命儒臣纂修遼、金、宋三史，右丞相脫脫以監修國史領都總裁，辟樞本府長史，力辭不拜。
units.en: In Zhizheng 3 the court ordered the compilation of the Liao, Jin, and Song histories; Toghto, as chief compiler, invited Shu to serve as his chief clerk, but Shu firmly declined.
units.literal: In the third year of Zhizheng, Confucian ministers were ordered to compile the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song; Right Grand Councilor Toghto as overseer of national history led the general chief compiler and recruited Shu as chief clerk of his headquarters—he strenuously declined and did not accept the post.

units.zh: 七年，申命史臣纂修本朝后妃、功臣傳，復以翰林修撰、儒林郎、同知制誥兼國史院編修官召樞，俾與討論，复避不就。
units.en: In the seventh year the court again ordered biographies of empresses and meritorious subjects of the dynasty; Shu was again summoned as Hanlin compiler and History Office editor to join the work, but again he declined.
units.literal: In the seventh year, again ordering history ministers to compile this dynasty's empresses and meritorious subjects' biographies, again summoning Shu as Hanlin compiler, Forest of Scholars Gentleman, Associate Proclaimer of Edicts and concurrent History Office compiler, to have him join discussion—again he avoided and did not go.

units.zh: 使者強之行，至杭州，固辭而歸。
units.en: Envoys pressed him to go; at Hangzhou he firmly refused and returned home.
units.literal: The envoys forced him to go; reaching Hangzhou, he firmly declined and returned.

units.zh: 嘗著《春秋三傳歸一義》三十卷，《刊定三國志》六十五卷，《林下竊議》、《曲江張公年譜》各一卷，《敝帚編》若干卷。
units.en: His works included Unified Meanings of the Three Spring and Autumn Commentaries (30 juan), Collated Records of the Three Kingdoms (65 juan), Private Discussions under the Forest and Annual Biography of Lord Zhang of Qujiang (1 juan each), and Broom-Ends Collection (several juan).
units.literal: He once authored Unified Meanings of the Three Spring and Autumn Commentaries in thirty juan, Collated Records of the Three Kingdoms in sixty-five juan, Private Discussions under the Forest and Annual Biography of Lord Zhang of Qujiang each one juan, and Broom-Ends Collection in several juan.

units.zh: 至正八年卒，年五十有七。
units.en: He died in Zhizheng 8 at the age of fifty-seven.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Zhizheng he died, age fifty-seven.

units.zh: 孫轍，字履常，其先自金陵徙家臨川。
units.en: Sun Che, courtesy name Lüchang, came from a family that had moved from Jinling to Linchuan.
units.literal: Sun Che, style name Lüchang, his ancestors moved their family from Jinling to Linchuan.

units.zh: 轍幼孤，母蔡氏教之，知警策自樹立。
units.en: Che lost his father young; his mother, Lady Cai, raised him, and he learned early to discipline himself and stand on his own.
units.literal: Che in youth was orphaned; his mother the Lady Cai taught him; he knew to be alert and spur himself and establish himself.

units.zh: 比長，學行純篤，事母甚孝。
units.en: When grown, his learning and conduct were pure and steadfast, and he was deeply filial toward his mother.
units.literal: When he had grown, learning and conduct were pure and earnest; he served his mother with great filial piety.

units.zh: 家居教授，門庭蕭然，而考德問業者日盛。
units.en: He taught at home in modest circumstances, yet students seeking moral instruction and learning grew daily.
units.literal: Dwelling at home he taught; his gate and courtyard were austere, yet those examining virtue and inquiring into studies daily increased.

units.zh: 郡中俊彥有聲者皆出其門。
units.en: The county's most promising scholars all came from his school.
units.literal: The commandery's outstanding talents of renown all came from his gate.

units.zh: 轍與人言，一以孝弟忠信為本，辭溫氣和，聞者莫不油然感悟。
units.en: In conversation Che always grounded his words in filial piety, fraternity, loyalty, and trust; his tone was gentle and harmonious, and listeners were invariably moved.
units.literal: When Che spoke with people, he took filial piety, brotherly duty, loyalty, and trustworthiness as his root; his words were warm and his air harmonious—listeners none failed to be richly moved to perception.

units.zh: 待親戚鄉里禮意周洽，言論間未嘗幾微及人過失長短。
units.en: He treated relatives and neighbors with full courtesy and never spoke, even in passing, of others' faults.
units.literal: Toward kin and village his ritual intent was thorough and harmonious; in discourse he never in the slightest touched others' faults, long or short.

units.zh: 士子至郡者必來見，部使者長吏以下仁且賢者，必造焉。
units.en: Scholars passing through the prefecture always called on him, as did circuit envoys and local officials who were humane and worthy.
units.literal: Scholars arriving in the commandery all came to see him; circuit envoys, magistrates, and below who were benevolent and worthy—all must visit him.

units.zh: 轍樂易莊敬，接之以禮，言不及官府。
units.en: Che was affable yet dignified, received guests with proper courtesy, and never spoke of official affairs.
units.literal: Che was cheerful and easy, grave and respectful, receiving people with ritual; his words did not reach to government offices.

units.zh: 憲司屢辟，皆不就。
units.en: The surveillance commission repeatedly invited him to office, but he always declined.
units.literal: The surveillance commission repeatedly recruited him—all he did not accept.

units.zh: 江西行省特以遺逸舉轍一人。
units.en: The Jiangxi Branch Secretariat specially nominated Che as a recluse.
units.literal: The Jiangxi Branch Secretariat specially recommended Che alone as a leftover recluse.

units.zh: 轍善為文章，吳澄嘗敘其集曰；
units.en: Che was a fine writer; Wu Cheng once wrote in the preface to his collected works:
units.literal: Che was skilled at literary compositions; Wu Cheng once prefaced his collected works, saying:

units.zh: 「所謂仁義之人，其言藹如也。」
units.en: "'The man of benevolence and righteousness—his words are gentle and kind.'"
units.literal: "What is called the person of benevolence and righteousness—his words are genial indeed."

units.zh: 其見稱許如此。
units.en: Such was the praise he won.
units.literal: Such was the praise he received.

units.zh: 元統二年，年七十有三，卒於家。
units.en: In Yuantong 2 he died at home at the age of seventy-three.
units.literal: In the second year of Yuantong, age seventy-three, he died at home.

units.zh: 同郡吳定翁字仲谷，其先當宋初自金陵來徙。
units.en: Wu Dingweng of the same prefecture, courtesy name Zhonggu, came from a family that had moved from Jinling in early Song times.
units.literal: In the same commandery, Wu Dingweng, style name Zhonggu, his ancestors at the beginning of Song came from Jinling to move here.

units.zh: 定翁幼歲儼如成人，寒暑衣冠不少懈，清修文雅，與孫轍齊名。
units.en: From childhood Dingweng conducted himself like an adult, never neglecting proper dress in any season; pure and refined, he was famed alongside Sun Che.
units.literal: Dingweng in youth was solemn as an adult; in cold and heat his cap and robes slackened not at all; pure cultivation and refined elegance—he shared fame with Sun Che.

units.zh: 而最善為詩，揭
units.en: He was especially gifted in poetry; Jie
units.literal: Yet he was most skilled at poetry; Jie

units.zh: 傒斯稱其幽茂疏淡，可比盧摯。
units.en: Xisi praised his verse as secluded, lush, and spare—comparable to Lu Zhi.
units.literal: Xisi praised its secluded lushness, sparse and light, comparable to Lu Zhi.

units.zh: 御史及江西之方伯牧守部使者，辟薦相望，終身不為動。
units.en: Censors and Jiangxi officials repeatedly recommended him, but he never wavered through his life.
units.literal: Censors and Jiangxi's regional lords, prefects, magistrates, and circuit envoys—recruitment and recommendation looked on each other in succession; through his life he was not moved.

units.zh: 程鉅夫嘗貽書曰：「臨川士友及門者，踵相接也，何相望足下耿耿如玉人，而不可得見乎！」
units.en: Cheng Jufu once wrote to him: "Scholar friends in Linchuan and students at my gate come in endless succession—why is it that one so pure as jade as yourself remains beyond my sight!"
units.literal: Cheng Jufu once sent a letter saying: "Linchuan's scholar friends and those at the gate follow heel to heel—why gazing at you, sir, bright and clear as a jade man, yet unable to obtain a meeting!"

units.zh: 定翁嘗曰；
units.en: Dingweng once said:
units.literal: Dingweng once said:

units.zh: 「士無求用於世，惟求無愧于世。」
units.en: "A scholar should not seek to be employed by the world, only to have no shame before it."
units.literal: "A gentleman does not seek to be used by the world; he only seeks to have no shame before the world."

units.zh: 人以為名言。
units.en: People regarded this as a memorable maxim.
units.literal: People took this as a famous saying.

units.zh: 何中，字太虛，撫之樂安人。
units.en: He Zhong, courtesy name Taixu, was from Le'an in Fu prefecture.
units.literal: He Zhong, style name Taixu, was a man of Le'an in Fu.

units.zh: 少穎拔，以古學自任，家有藏書萬卷，手自校讎。
units.en: Bright and precocious in youth, he devoted himself to classical learning; his family owned ten thousand volumes, which he collated with his own hand.
units.literal: In youth sharp and outstanding, he took ancient learning as his charge; his household had ten thousand juan of stored books, which he personally collated.

units.zh: 其學弘深該博，廣平程鉅夫，清河元明善，柳城姚燧，東平王構，同郡吳澄、揭傒斯，皆推服之。
units.en: His learning was broad and profound; Cheng Jufu of Guangping, Yuan Mingshan of Qinghe, Yao Sui of Liucheng, Wang Gou of Dongping, and his fellow townsman Wu Cheng and Jie Xisi all held him in esteem.
units.literal: His learning was vast, deep, and comprehensive; Guangping's Cheng Jufu, Qinghe's Yuan Mingshan, Liucheng's Yao Sui, Dongping's Wang Gou, and in the same commandery Wu Cheng and Jie Xisi—all pushed forward and submitted to him.

units.zh: 至順二年，江西行省平章全岳柱聘為龍興郡學師。
units.en: In Zhishun 2, Grand Councilor Quan Yuezhu of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat appointed him teacher at the Longxing prefectural school.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhishun, Jiangxi Branch Secretariat Grand Councilor Quan Yuezhu engaged him as teacher of the Longxing commandery school.

units.zh: 明年六月，以疾卒。
units.en: He died of illness the following sixth month.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the next year, he died of illness.

units.zh: 所著有《易類象》二卷、《書傳補遺》十卷、《通鑑綱目測海》三卷、《知非堂稿》十七卷。
units.en: His works included Images of the Changes Categories (2 juan), Supplementary Remnants of the Documents Tradition (10 juan), Fathoming the Sea of the Comprehensive Mirror Outline (3 juan), and Drafts from the Hall of Knowing Error (17 juan).
units.literal: Works he authored include Images of the Changes Categories in two juan, Supplementary Remnants of the Documents Tradition in ten juan, Fathoming the Sea of the Comprehensive Mirror Outline in three juan, and Drafts from the Hall of Knowing Error in seventeen juan.

units.zh: 同郡危復之，字見心。
units.en: Wei Fuzhi of the same prefecture, courtesy name Jianxin.
units.literal: In the same commandery, Wei Fuzhi, style name Jianxin.

units.zh: 宋末為太學生，師事湯漢，博覽群書，好讀《易》，尤工於詩。
units.en: At the end of the Song he was an Imperial University student under Tang Han, read widely, loved the Changes, and was especially accomplished in poetry.
units.literal: At the end of Song he was an Imperial University student, studied under Tang Han, broadly read the many books, loved reading the Changes, and was especially skilled at poetry.

units.zh: 至元初，元帥郭昂屢薦為儒學官，不就。
units.en: Early in the Zhiyuan era Marshal Guo Ang repeatedly recommended him for a Confucian office, but he declined.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhiyuan, Marshal Guo Ang repeatedly recommended him as Confucian learning official—he did not accept.

units.zh: 至元中，朝廷累遣奉御察罕及翰林應奉詹玉以幣征之，皆弗起。
units.en: During Zhiyuan the court repeatedly sent Palace Attendant Chahan and Hanlin Attendant Zhan Yu with gifts to summon him, but he never accepted.
units.literal: In the middle of Zhiyuan, the court repeatedly sent Palace Attendant Chahan and Hanlin Attendant Zhan Yu with gifts to summon him—all he did not rise.

units.zh: 隱於紫霞山中，士友私諡曰貞白先生。
units.en: He lived in seclusion on Purple Clouds Mountain; friends privately styled him Master Pure White (Zhenbai).
units.literal: He hid in the Purple Clouds Mountains; scholar friends privately gave him the posthumous style Master Pure White.

units.zh: 武恪，字伯威，宣德府人。
units.en: Wu Ke, courtesy name Bowei, was from Xuande Prefecture.
units.literal: Wu Ke, style name Bowei, was a man of Xuande Prefecture.

units.zh: 初以神童遊學江南，吳澄為江西儒學副提舉，薦入國學肄業。
units.en: Known early as a child prodigy, he studied in the south; Wu Cheng, as Jiangxi vice commissioner for Confucian learning, recommended him to the National University.
units.literal: At first as a child prodigy he traveled to study in Jiangnan; Wu Cheng as Jiangxi Vice Commissioner for Confucian Learning recommended him to enter the National University for study.

units.zh: 明宗在潛邸，選恪為說書秀才，及出鎮雲南，恪在行。
units.en: While Mingzong was still in his princely residence he chose Ke as lecturing scholar; when Mingzong went to govern Yunnan, Ke accompanied him.
units.literal: When Mingzong was in his princely residence, he selected Ke as lecturing scholar; when he went out to garrison Yunnan, Ke was in the entourage.

units.zh: 明宗欲起兵陝西，恪諫曰：「太子北行，於國有君命，於家有叔父之命，今若向京師發一箭，史官必書太子反。」
units.en: When Mingzong planned to raise troops in Shaanxi, Ke admonished him: "The crown prince travels north with the emperor's command and his uncle's authority; if you now loose a single arrow toward the capital, the historians will record that the crown prince rebelled."
units.literal: Mingzong wished to raise troops in Shaanxi; Ke remonstrated: "The crown prince goes north—toward the state there is the ruler's command, toward the family there is the uncle's command; now if you shoot a single arrow toward the capital, the history officers will surely write 'the crown prince rebelled.'"

units.zh: 左右惡恪言，乃曰：「武秀才有母在京，合遣其回。」
units.en: His attendants, resenting Ke's counsel, said, "Scholar Wu has a mother in the capital and should be sent home."
units.literal: Those at his side hated Ke's words and said: "Scholar Wu has a mother in the capital—it is fitting to send him back."

units.zh: 恪遂還京師，居陋巷，教訓子弟。
units.en: Ke returned to the capital, lived in a humble lane, and taught his sons and disciples.
units.literal: Ke thereupon returned to the capital, dwelt in a mean lane, and taught and instructed sons and younger kin.

units.zh: 文宗知其名，除秘書監典簿。
units.en: Wenzong knew his reputation and appointed him registrar of the Secretariat Directorate.
units.literal: Wenzong knew his name and appointed him Secretariat Directorate registrar.

units.zh: 秩滿，丁內艱，再除中瑞司典簿，改汾西縣尹，皆不起。
units.en: When his term ended he mourned his mother; he was again offered registrar of the Central Auspicious Office and then magistrate of Fenxi County, but accepted neither.
units.literal: When his term ended, he entered mourning for his mother; again appointed Central Auspicious Office registrar, transferred to magistrate of Fenxi County—all he did not rise to.

units.zh: 人或勸之仕，恪曰：「向為親屈，今親已死，不復仕矣。」
units.en: When others urged him to serve, Ke said, "I took office before only for my parent's sake; now that my parent is dead, I will not serve again."
units.literal: When some urged him to take office, Ke said: "Formerly I bent for my parent's sake; now my parent is dead—I will not serve again."

units.zh: 居數歲，會朝廷選守令，泰不華舉恪為平陽沁水縣尹，亦不赴。
units.en: Some years later, when the court was selecting local officials, Tai Buhua recommended him as magistrate of Qinshui in Pingyang, but he again declined.
units.literal: After dwelling several years, it happened the court was selecting prefects and magistrates; Tai Buhua recommended Ke as magistrate of Qinshui County in Pingyang—again he did not go.

units.zh: 近臣又薦為授經郎，恪遂陽為喑啞，不就。
units.en: A court intimate again recommended him as Classics Lecturer; Ke then feigned muteness and refused.
units.literal: A close minister again recommended him as Classics Lecturer; Ke thereupon pretended to be mute and did not accept.

units.zh: 恪好讀《周易》，每日堅坐。
units.en: Ke loved the Zhou Changes and sat in daily meditation.
units.literal: Ke loved reading the Zhou Changes; daily he sat firmly in meditation.

units.zh: 或問之曰：「先生之學，以何為本？」
units.en: Someone asked him, "Master, what is the foundation of your learning?"
units.literal: Someone asked him: "Master, in your learning, what is taken as root?"

units.zh: 恪曰：「以敬為本。」
units.en: He answered, "Reverence."
units.literal: Ke said: "Reverence is taken as root."

units.zh: 所著有《水雲集》若干卷。
units.en: His works included Water and Clouds Collection in several juan.
units.literal: Works he authored include Water and Clouds Collection in several juan.

units.zh: 其從之學者多有所成，佛家奴為太尉，完者不花僉樞密院事，皆有賢名。
units.en: Many of his students attained distinction: Fo Jianu became Grand Marshal and Wan Zhebu Hua became associate administrator of the Privy Council—men of worthy reputation.
units.literal: Many of those who followed him in study achieved success; Fo Jianu became Grand Marshal, Wan Zhebu Hua became associate administrator of the Privy Council—all had worthy names.
